subject: Re: MAP — performance benchmarking metrics and triage plan
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena@fastretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Matt O'Neal <matt.oneal@fastretail.com>
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: MAP kickoff: performance baseline data we need

Marissa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — FastRetail's engineering team wants a concrete MAP that includes the performance benchmarking plan and acceptance criteria. High level asks:

- Baseline latency (p50/p95), TTFT, and throughput at our expected concurrency (up to 250 concurrent inference sessions).
- Reproducible harness & scripts so we can compare Redwood vs our incumbent provider.
- Clear instrumentation points (client-side vs server-side) to avoid apples-to-oranges results.
- Proposed close timeline: we'd like to finalize vendor selection by end of Q1.

Can you send a proposed MAP and the benchmark methodology by EOD Friday?

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Platform Engineering, FastRetail
[attachment: FR_requirements.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@fastretail.com>
Cc: Prioym Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 05 Feb 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: performance baseline data we need

Elena —

Appreciate the clarity. I've attached a first-pass MAP that includes milestones, owners, and an initial benchmark plan. Quick summary of what we'll deliver by Friday:

1) Benchmark harness (bash + python) + sample payloads to run locally/in your cloud.
2) Measurement definitions: p50/p95 latency (server-side), TTFT (time to first token at client), steady-state throughput (tokens/sec), and end-to-end latency under concurrency.
3) Two test modalities:
   - Deterministic throughput: greedy/argmax decoding to stress tokens/sec.
   - Representative quality run: same sampling temperature and top-k you use in prod (to validate TTFT costs).
4) Repro steps to align tokenizer and model variant.

Attachments: FastRetail_MAP_v1.xlsx, redwood_benchmark_harness.sh, sample_payloads.json

I'll loop Prioym from Solutions who will own the test scripts and Monica from Security for any data handling notes. Proposed close timeline in the MAP: vendor decision 2026-03-01, pilot in-production by 2026-04-15. Happy to compress if you need it earlier.

Next step: can you confirm the sequence-length distribution for your traffic (median/95th) and whether you apply aggressive prefix caching at the gateway? That drives our batching and model selection.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[attachment: FastRetail_MAP_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Prioym Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@fastretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 06 Feb 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: benchmark harness + methodology (details)

Hi Elena —

Attached is the benchmark harness and a short README inside the repo. Key methodology notes (please review so we align):

- Test hardware: we'll provide both hosted runs (Redwood Dedicated) and a containerized harness you can run in your AWS account. Please run the container on a p4d.24xlarge equivalent instance for parity.
- Model variants: we'll test the 8k and 32k context variants, both fp16 and int8-quant runs.
- Inputs: use the attached sample_payloads.json; we will also accept a 1k-sample dataset you send.
- Metrics captured: server p50/p95 latency (in ms, excluding network egress), TTFT measured from client send to first token received, throughput measured at steady state (tokens/sec), concurrency ramp (50,100,150,200,250).
- Warmup: we recommend a 5-minute steady warmup per concurrency level to mitigate cold-starts and JIT artifacts.
- Batching & queueing: we will publish the batch-size distributions the runtime used during each test. Make sure you disable any gateway-level request coalescing on your side for the parity run.

Common discrepancy traps:
- Tokenization mismatch (different tokenizer versions or pre-tokenized inputs).
- Different stopping criteria or decode settings (sampling vs greedy).
- Hidden proxies / client retries inflating TTFT.
- Measuring client-side vs server-side timing incorrectly.

Action items for FastRetail:
1) Confirm sequence-length distribution CSV by EOD Monday.
2) Provide a 1k representative sample dataset (anonymized).
3) If possible, schedule a 1-hour alignment call next week to walk the harness and verify run commands.

Attachments: redwood_benchmark_harness.sh, sample_payloads.json

Cheers,
Prioym Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_benchmark_harness.sh (sh)]

From: Elena Torres <elena@fastretail.com>
To: Prioym Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Matt O'Neal <matt.oneal@fastretail.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Feb 2026 10:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: benchmark harness + methodology (details)

Prioym —

Thanks. We've run the initial harness in our environment and are seeing a consistent mismatch vs your hosted numbers: our p95 latency is ~20% higher, and TTFT is 35–40% worse than your report for the same model/config. We followed the runbook and used greedy decoding; tokenizer versions match. My team captured the run logs and attached a short summary (see inline below).

Inline findings:
- Hardware: running on p4d equivalent, hyperthreading enabled by default.
- Observed queueing: noticeable spike in queue length at concurrency 150+.
- Client network RTT: average 12ms to Redwood endpoint.

Questions we have:
1) Could your hosted environment be using kernel/tuning or a different batch sizing policy that skews steady-state throughput?
2) Do you have recommended runtime flags to disable request coalescing on your side so we can emulate exact behavior?

We still want to progress but need a path to close the methodology gap before we sign.

Thanks,
Elena
[attachment: FR_run_summary.csv (csv)]

From: Prioym Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Torres <elena@fastretail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP kickoff: benchmark harness + methodology (discrepancy triage)

Elena —

Thanks for the logs and summary — good reproduction work. Quick triage notes after an initial pass:

1) Kernel/network tuning: our Dedicated clusters apply NIC interrupt moderation and tuned kernel settings for lower syscalls per packet; this reduces CPU overhead and can show as 10–15% lower p95 in hosted runs. We'll provide the exact sysctl knobs and a container image with the same network stack you can run in your infra to replicate.

2) Batching policy: your observed queueing at 150+ suggests your local harness is letting requests accumulate into occasionally large batches which increases p95 for single-request latency. For parity, run the harness with --max-batch=32 and --latency-sla-ms=120 to prioritize latency over token throughput.

3) Warmup & JIT: ensure you do a 5–10 minute warmup that includes representative prefix lengths. JIT variations can account for up to 8–12% variance on the p95 initially.

4) TTFT probes: your 12ms RTT is small but we measure TTFT from our ingress to first token — please run both client-measured and server-measured TTFT; differences will highlight network vs server decode time.

5) Competitive differences: if you want, we can run a head-to-head test (Redwood hosted vs incumbent) using your sample dataset and provide a side-by-side breakdown including batch-size distributions, kernel flags, and per-step timing. This is often the fastest way to build confidence.

Proposed next steps (short list):
- We will publish a Docker image with our kernel tunings and the harness by EOD Wednesday.
- You run a parity run with --max-batch=32 and share logs.
- We'll schedule a 60-minute troubleshooting session to go through traces (can be next Thu).

I'll also loop in Monica for any guidance on what can/should be disabled if FastRetail keeps data in flight during the runs.

Regards,
Prioym Das
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood_docker_with_tuning.tar.gz (tar.gz)]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Date: Sun, 15 Feb 2026 16:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: MAP — next steps and close timeline alignment

Team / Elena —

Thanks for the detailed reproduce work. From a deal-risk perspective, we should offer a short head-to-head run (hosted Redwood vs incumbent) using FastRetail's 1k sample and produce a single-slide summary that shows p50/p95, TTFT, tokens/sec, and batch-size distributions. If the variance persists we will:

- Share the exact kernel/sysctl settings and a prebuilt tuned Docker image.
- Provide a constrained SLA for p95 at target concurrency as part of the MAP (with a rollback clause).
- Offer a 30-day pilot credit if we need to run production-real traffic to validate steady-state.

Close timeline update in MAP: target signature date moved to 2026-03-08 to allow time for verification, pilot, and final procurement review.

Action items (owner):
- Prioym: deliver Docker image and runbook (ETA Wed).
- FastRetail: run parity harness with --max-batch=32 and share logs (ETA Fri).
- Marissa: update MAP with the new signature target and include the pilot credit language (ETA Tue).

Appreciate the partnership — we'll make sure the benchmarking path is airtight.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
